sections.html:
Hastings is the county seat of Adams County and sits roughly 14 miles south of Interstate 80. Much of the housing goes back to the railroad years, with a second wave of building during the war years.

Downtown burned in 1879 and was rebuilt, and growth picked up again from 1900 to 1930. Those decades left Craftsman, Prairie, Colonial Revival and American Foursquare houses. Heartwell Park and Central Hastings are two of the oldest neighborhoods and are on the National Register of Historic Places. Owners in those two districts should check with the city before starting exterior projects, since a review may apply.

sections.h2: Wartime houses and what buyers ask about them
sections.html:
The Naval Ammunition Depot, built in 1942, caused a housing shortage. The city grew from about 15,000 to 23,000 people in under a year, and existing houses were altered while new neighborhoods went up fast. An 840-unit village called Spencer Park was built for workers.

  • Houses from that push, and older ones altered to take in workers, may still have original wiring, plumbing or windows.
  • A buyer who finances may need repairs finished before the lender will fund the loan.
  • If you know the age of the house and any additions, you can fill in the disclosure form faster and leave fewer lines marked unknown.

The City of Hastings Building and Construction Inspection office covers the city limits and the extraterritorial jurisdiction. It has three inspectors, and it also staffs the Building Board of Appeals and takes complaints.

  • Contact an inspector before work that needs a permit, such as a roof tear-off, furnace swap or deck.
  • If a neighbor reports a safety concern about your structure, the same office handles it.
  • Missing permits usually come out once a buyer's lender or home inspector starts asking questions.

Request the permit history for your Hastings address. A permit that was never finalized, or an addition built with none, belongs in a written note to the buyer before signing. Call the office to ask whether any sale-time requirement applies to a single-family house.

sections.h2: Selling a Hastings house, step by step
sections.html:
Listing or direct offer, the paperwork runs in roughly the same order. Seeing it laid out before you start keeps a closing date from slipping.

  1. Get your parcel number and latest tax statement from the Adams County Treasurer, Suite 106 at the courthouse.
  2. Complete the Nebraska seller disclosure form early, writing "unknown" wherever you honestly do not know.
  3. Ask the Hastings inspection office whether any permits are still open on the property.
  4. Once you accept an offer, deliver the signed disclosure no later than the effective date of the binding contract.
  5. The title company searches title, clears liens and drafts the deed.
  6. You sign the deed at closing. It goes to the Register of Deeds for recording, and the stamp tax is deducted from your proceeds.

With a cash buyer there is no appraisal and no loan approval, so the final three steps can go quicker. The deed, the transfer statement and the recording still take place.

sections.h2: Where to record a deed and pay property tax
sections.html:
The Adams County Register of Deeds records deeds. Documents are scanned daily, so recorded papers can come back within 24 hours. The Treasurer bills real estate taxes on December 1 each year, and they are due December 31. First-half taxes become delinquent on May 1 of the next year and second-half taxes on September 1.

OfficeAddressPhone
Register of Deeds500 N. Denver Ave, Hastings402-461-7148
Treasurer500 West 4th St, Suite 106, Hastings402-461-7120

A replat is signed only after the current year's taxes are paid in full, and the Treasurer runs public and private tax sales for unpaid taxes.

Hastings sellers pay the state documentary stamp tax when the deed is recorded. The charge is $3.32 on each $1,000 of price, counting any fraction as a full $1,000, for deeds recorded July 18, 2026 or later. It was $2.32 before that. Check the Nebraska Department of Revenue for the figure in force on your closing date, and plan on the title company taking it out of your proceeds.

sections.h2: What a Hastings seller owes the buyer in writing
sections.html:
Selling a house with one to four units means giving the buyer a disclosure statement that you have signed. Deliver it no later than the effective date of a binding purchase contract, and correct it if anything on it turns out to be wrong before then.

You are not liable for an error outside your personal knowledge, and agents are not liable unless they knew. So an honest "unknown" protects you. Under Nebraska Revised Statute 76-2,120, a buyer who never got the statement has one year after taking possession or after the conveyance, whichever comes first, to bring a lawsuit.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale a good fit for a Hastings house?
sections.html:
A cash sale can suit a Hastings owner when time or condition makes a standard listing hard. Older homes, estate properties and tenant-occupied rentals often need work that a retail buyer would not want to finance.

Judge each route by your net. Subtract commissions, repair bills and the carrying costs of an empty house, including utilities and tax that keeps building toward December 31, then hold that figure up against a direct offer. We cannot promise a price. To start, send us the address and a few words about the situation.

sections.h2: If property tax is still owed
sections.html:
Statements go out December 1 and the full year is due December 31. The county treats the first half as late after May 1 of the following year, and the second half as late after September 1. Back taxes can land a parcel in a public or private tax sale handled by the Treasurer. If you owe, the title company settles the balance out of your sale proceeds at closing, so request a payoff figure before you say yes to an offer.

Have three things ready when you call the Treasurer at 402-461-7120: the parcel number, your name exactly as it reads on the deed, and the closing date you are aiming for. Thinking about a replat? The county signs it only after the current year's taxes are paid in full, so settle the bill first.

faqs.q: When are Adams County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: The county bills on December 1 and the year is due December 31. After that, the first half is late as of May 1 of the next year and the second half as of September 1.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Hastings?
faqs.a: Take it to the Adams County Register of Deeds, 500 N. Denver Avenue in Hastings, or call 402-461-7148. Scanned documents can be returned within 24 hours.

faqs.q: How much deed tax does the seller pay in Nebraska?
faqs.a: Sellers owe $3.32 per $1,000 of price, with any fraction rounded up, on deeds recorded July 18, 2026 or later.

faqs.q: Does the city inspect a house before it sells in Hastings?
faqs.a: The Hastings inspection office serves the city and its extraterritorial area, with three inspectors. Call the office to ask whether anything applies to a single-family sale.
Hastings Public Schools serves the city. Adams Central Junior-Senior High School, a rural public school, is just outside town.
